title: Wildcard Route Matcher
statement:
Design a slash-delimited URL route table that supports single-segment `*` wildcards and resolves the most specific matching handler.

Contract
- Construct an empty router with `new Solution()`.
- `register(pattern, handler)` registers `handler` (`handler` non-null and non-blank) for `pattern`. Re-registering the same normalized pattern overwrites its previous handler.
- `match(path)` returns the handler for the most specific registered pattern matching `path`, or `""` when no pattern matches.
- Every `pattern` and `path` must be non-null, start with `"/"`, and contain no empty internal segments (`"//"`); otherwise throw `IllegalArgumentException`. A single trailing slash on non-root paths is normalized away (`"/teams/"` and `"/teams"` both have segment `["teams"]`, while `"/"` has zero segments).
- In a pattern, segment `"*"` matches any single segment; every other segment matches only exact literal text. Patterns match only paths with the same segment count.
- If multiple patterns match `path`, prefer a **literal** segment over `"*"` at the earliest differing segment index from left to right.

Examples
- Registering `(/projects/*/issues -> listIssues)` and `(/projects/core/issues -> coreIssues)` resolves `/projects/core/issues` to `coreIssues` and `/projects/ops/issues` to `listIssues`.
- Registering `(/api/*/members -> wildcardFirst)` and `(/api/v1/* -> literalFirst)` resolves `/api/v1/members` to `literalFirst`.
- Registering `(/ -> home)` resolves `/` to `home` and `/unknown` to `""`.

examples.input: reg /projects/*/issues listIssues; reg /projects/core/issues coreIssues; match /projects/core/issues; match /projects/ops/issues

hints: Split normalized paths into segment arrays and store patterns in a segment-level trie rather than scanning every registered route.
Give each trie node a map of literal child segments plus one optional wildcard child node.

Search recursively segment by segment, trying the exact literal child before the wildcard child; the first branch that reaches a terminal handler automatically wins left-to-right specificity. Intended complexity across `n` operations of bounded segment depth: O(n) time and O(n) space.
inputSyntax: Input: semicolon-separated reg <pattern> <handler> and match <path>, for example: reg /projects/*/issues listIssues; reg /projects/core/issues coreIssues; match /projects/core/issues; match /projects/ops/issues
sampleInput: reg /projects/*/issues listIssues; reg /projects/core/issues coreIssues; match /projects/core/issues; match /projects/ops/issues
